metais limits — List every resource limit, with its default, unit and class.

Usage:
  metais limits [--json]

Examples:
  metais limits
      Prints the table of limits.
  metais limits --json
      Prints it as one metais.limits/1 document.

Every size, count and ratio metais reads, computes or writes is bounded, and
every bound has a name and a default. A package within every package limit is
portable: every conforming tool accepts it at the defaults. A limit may be
lowered for one run, and is never raised.

A default in bytes is shown in the largest of KiB, MiB and GiB (powers of 1024)
that it is a whole number of; --json gives every default as a number in the
limit's unit.

Flags:
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  A table of every limit: its name, default, unit (bytes, count or ratio) and
  class (package, data or work), in the specification's order. With --json, one
  metais.limits/1 document.

Refusals:
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais limits --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais limits --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais limits --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais limits --help
